integrationRules: This manifest indexes authority; it does not reorder it.
A missing entry in this manifest does not demote a higher-authority named source.
The primary authority remains the human-readable integration entrypoint until explicitly superseded.
Generator/runtime code may use this manifest for discoverability but must still obey field-level provenance/status.
DERIVED and PROPOSED documents remain subordinate even when listed here.
Race/vessel-specific material outranks generic embodiment only within its documented scope.
Current runtime behavior is authoritative for implementation behavior, not automatically for setting-wide historical canon.

Physical gravity and curvature packets must preserve SI units, reference-frame identity, potential reference, model validity, uncertainty, and provenance before versioned normalization or family-specific transit response is applied.

When time-dependent authoritative source states are supplied, their source epoch, target epoch, reference frame, velocity, covariance ancestry and propagation-model identity must be preserved before the physical route sampler consumes their propagated positions.
Missing source velocity is unresolved motion rather than zero velocity, and missing covariance is unresolved uncertainty rather than perfect certainty.

Linear or constant-acceleration source propagation must carry an explicit approximation-validity bound; exceeding a declared position/velocity tolerance is OUTSIDE_MODEL_VALIDITY and requires higher-fidelity dynamics rather than a larger finite route-severity score.
Forward white-acceleration process-noise formulas may not be naively reused for backward propagation; reverse-time stochastic propagation requires an explicit model or process-noise covariance.
Independent per-source covariance packets do not establish independent source errors; known cross-source or barycentric covariance must remain explicit.

Time-aware route generation must distinguish ROUTE_EPOCH_SNAPSHOT, CONTINUOUS_PROJECTED_PROGRESS, PRECOMMIT_ENDPOINT and ANCHORED_PORTAL semantics; nonlocal operators may not acquire a fabricated local superluminal traversal velocity.

Adaptive spatiotemporal refinement may increase evidence density when gravity, encounter time, covariance, source motion, tidal eigenvalues, acceleration direction, or tracked tidal axes change too rapidly, but a numerical sample ceiling is never proof of convergence or safety.
Tidal eigenvector sign is gauge freedom. Branch rotation must be sign-invariant, and numerical sign flips may not be reported as physical 180-degree rotations.
Raw eigenvalue sorting is not sufficient for tidal branch identity. Non-degenerate branches must be continuity-matched across samples using eigenvector overlap or a higher-fidelity equivalent.

Near repeated tidal eigenvalues, individual eigenvectors inside the degenerate eigenspace are not physically unique. The degenerate subspace must be preserved as such rather than promoted to an arbitrary canonical direction.

Tidal eigenaxes and their rotations are ordinary gravitational evidence; they may inform a versioned Gravitational Plane or Slipstream/Shear response model but do not themselves prove that a fictional lane, fork, or boundary exists.

When an authoritative physicalEnvironmentContext is supplied, route safety must use the physical gravity/curvature bridge; a PARTIAL, UNRESOLVED, or OUTSIDE_MODEL_VALIDITY physical result may not be replaced by a PROPOSED route archetype fallback.
Only absence of a physicalEnvironmentContext permits the existing PROPOSED route archetype environment fallback.
A physical route path must preserve every sampled field-point result and its provenance; route-wide extrema are sampled extrema unless a convergence or analytic bound proves otherwise.

Published-first EXAMPLE route sampling must consume blacklight-exo-source-authority.js rather than maintaining a competing mass/position table; candidate and disputed bodies remain excluded from confirmed gravitational totals.
Catalog/system coordinates are reference positions, not canonical FTL emergence points; path sampling must not evaluate an endpoint singularity and relabel it as route physics.
Missing source velocity, physical radius, route epoch, or covariance remains missing. Physical route sampling may return PARTIAL and may not silently substitute zero or perfect certainty.
Adaptive path refinement thresholds are numerical engineering parameters, not constants of nature, and their identity must remain attached to any route result that depends on them.
Route-wide safety is conjunctive across required path segments; averaging benign samples may not erase a blocked or catastrophic segment.

Each required physical route interval must retain its own environment envelope, finite-difference diagnostics, model-validity state, uncertainty and provenance; a route-level summary may not replace interval evidence.
PARTIAL physical interval evidence remains unresolved for certification unless a higher-fidelity source closes the missing fields; missing evidence is not zero uncertainty.
Finite-difference route gradients are numerical diagnostics rather than exact spatial derivatives unless convergence or analytic reasoning establishes the derivative interpretation.

Each physically valid route interval must pass through the selected family-specific normalization, uncertainty, efficiency, observability, lookahead and recovery gates before the route is family-certified; a route-level family average is prohibited.

For exotic families, an absent family-boundary hazard is unresolved unless the channel is explicitly established as known absent; ordinary gravitational metrics may not manufacture or silently zero an operator-specific boundary term.
The earliest blocking family-specific interval must remain visible together with distance/time-to-block and intervention reachability; later benign intervals cannot hide it.

The first-blocker presentation layer is downstream of certification and may format or visualize certified interval evidence, but it may not recompute gravity, normalization, family response, observability, recovery, or intervention reach.
The first-blocker presentation must verify the certified firstBlockingSegmentIndex against ordered blocking intervals; disagreement is CONFLICT and may not be silently repaired by UI code.
Corridor interval display width represents route-fraction span rather than hazard severity, and no presentation-only synthetic safety percentage may replace conjunctive certification.
Continuous projected-progress reachability and PRECOMMIT decision-horizon reachability are distinct models and may not be collapsed by inventing a local superluminal velocity for nonlocal operators.

Physical quantities with unlike dimensions must be divided by explicit versioned reference scales before they enter a combined dimensionless family-severity model; those reference scales are calibration, not constants of nature.
Coordinate gravitational acceleration, proper acceleration, tidal loading, and spacetime curvature are distinct quantities and may not be silently substituted for one another.

Weak-field potential, acceleration, and Newtonian tidal tensors may be superposed within their approximation; exact general-relativistic curvature invariants may not be linearly superposed and presented as an exact multi-body spacetime.
OUTSIDE_MODEL_VALIDITY is a blocking modelling result. It may not be converted into an ordinary finite gravity-severity score merely to keep a route selectable.
Real-physics environmental calculations constrain fictional operator models but do not prove an FTL family is physically realizable or assign that family to a named race, vessel, or manufacturer.
Family-boundary hazard remains an operator-specific fictional term and may not be inferred from ordinary gravity metrics alone.
Calibration profile identity and version and any physical-normalization profile identity/version must be retained by a numerical safety certificate that depends on them.
Generated capability and route safety certification are separate outputs; REJECTED, UNRESOLVED, and CONFLICT states may not be flattened into ordinary certified performance.
The live EXO FTL certification UI must preserve the generated family when the family selector is random and must embed the route-safety certificate in exported dossiers.
The live EXO FTL route selector must visibly retain certification state for every evaluated route and guard blocked alternatives without erasing the failed selected route needed for diagnosis.

The safety-envelope presentation must expose gravity retention, calculation retention, actionable lookahead, recovery reserve, and hazard observability as separate constraints rather than averaging them into a synthetic safety percentage.

Control/navigation/maintenance embodiment may change how safety information is sensed, represented, actuated and serviced, but it may not discard any invariant safety channel required by the transit family.
Named race and vessel control embodiments must retain unresolved transit-family status unless a higher-authority source establishes the association.
Alien-to-human interface translation must preserve native-state provenance and may not convert unresolved state into safe/default values.
The live EXO FTL dossier must not default an unspecified operative technology basis to terrestrial machinery; unspecified basis is an explicit UNRESOLVED embodiment state.

Changing operative technology basis may change navigation representation, sensing, control, abort, maintenance, service environment and failure signatures, but may not change the generated or certified FTL family.
Complete dossier exports must keep generated performance, route certification, route matrix and control embodiment as distinguishable records with provenance rather than destructively merging them.
Technology ancestry must keep owner, operator, manufacturer, inventor and engineering origin distinct unless an authoritative source explicitly unifies them.

A race/species or polity name alone may not auto-populate an operative technology basis; live auto-resolution requires exactly one materially participating CONFIRMED basis or a higher-authority exact mapping.
Multiple materially participating CONFIRMED technology bases must remain CONFIRMED_MULTI/MULTI_BASIS rather than being collapsed to a majority basis.
Captured, imported, licensed, salvaged and reverse-engineered machinery must retain source ancestry through export and maintenance/certification workflows.
Technology ancestry cannot assign an FTL family; family authority remains independent.
